reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) describes high-temperature synthesis and entropy stabilization of HEA nanoparticles but provides no data on elemental segregation, surface melting, or differential mobilities during heating. The key mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the passages.
premises: Lower-melting-point elements (notably Cu) segregate to the nanoparticle surface upon heating
This segregation forms a disordered, liquid-like interfacial layer that nucleates complete melting
High configurational entropy of the core delays full segregation
Rapid cooling consolidates the transient layer into a homogeneous solid solution
Single-metal or binary nanoparticles lack such differential mobility and do not form a graded premelting regime
